_help.units: Distances and sizes are in tiles (1 tile = one grass square). Speeds are tiles per second. Times are seconds.
_help.reload: Save this file and reload the page to apply changes.
_help.flowers.kind: single = homing seed, beam = instant hit, bolt = piercing fireball in a line, cloud = poison cloud (damage is per stack per second), pulse = hits everything in range, chomp = bite (small critters are swallowed whole).
_help.flowers.slow: slow = speed multiplier while slowed (lower = slower), slowSeconds = how long it lasts after each pulse; perLevel.slowDuration adds that share of slowSeconds per level.
_help.flowers.pierce: Fire Lily fireballs hit at most this many monsters each (perLevel.pierce more per level).
_help.flowers.flyerDamage: Daisy seeds do this many times their damage to flying monsters.
_help.flowers.bossDamage: Sunflower beams do this many times their damage to bosses: they are the boss killers.
_help.flowers.maxHpBite: Snapdragon bites also take this share of the target's max health (bossMaxHpBite on bosses), so big monsters lose big chunks.
_help.enemies.poisonImmune: Stinkbloom poison doesn't affect it (and Stinkblooms don't aim at it).
_help.flowers.target: first = enemy furthest along the path (default), strong = of the tough monsters (at least toughShare of the toughest one's max health), the one closest to the cottage, big = the toughest enemy (highest max health), the one furthest along if several are as tough. Flowers that reach the whole map (Sunflower) spread their shots out at the start of each wave instead of all firing at once.
_help.flowerLevels.prices: A flower's cost is its base price. Planting it (seedling to level 1) costs cost x plantPrice; going from level L to L+1 costs cost x upgradeCostMultipliers[L-1] x upgradePrice. Healing is priced off the base cost (fullHealCostFraction). Planting and upgrade prices are rounded to the nearest priceStep (never below one step).
_help.flowerLevels.perLevel: Bonus added per level above 1, e.g. damage 0.5 means +50% damage per level.
_help.flowerLevels.wearPerSecond: Health every flower loses per second while a wave is running (the same for all flower types, none between waves), times wearMultiplierByLevel for its level. Flowers have 100 health; upgrading refills it.
_help.enemies.bite: Damage per second an enemy does to the cottage while chomping on it (it keeps chomping until killed).
_help.enemies.eats: Aphids stop to chew flowers near the road: damagePerSecond for chewSeconds, then rest for cooldown. One aphid per flower at a time, and higher-level flowers take less (wearMultiplierByLevel; max level is immune).
_help.enemies.size: Radius in tiles. 'light' enemies can be knocked back by the baton and swallowed by Snapdragons.
_help.intros: The warning shown the first time each monster type turns up in a game: [title, hint]. Leave a type out to skip its warning.
_help.difficulty.spawn: spawnGap = seconds between single monsters (random between the two), shrinking by spawnSpeedupPerWave each wave down to spawnGapMinScale of it. packGrowthPerWave makes packs (swarms, wasps) that much bigger every wave after they appear, up to packMaxGrowth times their size; every member costs its share of the wave budget (cost / group), so bigger packs come less often instead of adding monsters for free. openingRush = the share of each wave that pours out right at the start. newEnemyBoost multiplies how often a monster type appears in its first two waves; after that older types fade by oldEnemyFade per wave down to oldEnemyMin, so every wave feels different.
_help.difficulty: Enemy health = base * enemyHp * (1 + hpGrowth)^(wave-1): every wave, endless ones too, is hpGrowth tougher than the one before, with no jumps, so a full garden meets a clear wall. Wave size budget = waveBudgetBase + waveBudgetPerWave*wave + waveBudgetPerWaveSquared*wave^2. Both grow slowly at first and steeply towards the last waves. Every bossEvery-th wave has a boss; the one on the last wave has finalBossHp times more health. In endless mode the wave right after that big boss is a breather: breatherWaveSize times as many monsters, and no opening rush. After it, endless waves barely grow in number: the size budget is the last wave's times (1 + endlessWaveSizePerWave per wave past it); health keeps following hpGrowth. Every bossEvery waves into endless, each boss wave brings endlessBossesPerCycle more bosses; ordinary waves get them too, but bossFreeCycles cycles later (with 1: wave 15 has 2 bosses, 16-19 none, 20 has 3, 21-24 one each, 25 has 4, 26-29 two each). Endless bosses have endlessBossHp times the health they would otherwise have. Each boss is picked at random from bossTypes (by weight).
_help.difficulty.hard: Hard mode, switched on the pick screen (plant key on the map row): monsters have enemyHp times the health, waveSize times as many come, and each drops coins times as many coins (so the bigger crowds don't pay more). Made for experienced players whose gardens hold Normal with lots to spare.
_help.economy.coopCoinShare: In co-op, the share of every coin picked up that is split evenly between all cats (1 = fully shared, 0 = whoever picks it up keeps it).
_help.economy.entranceCoins: Coins monsters drop are multiplied by (entrances / 2) ^ entranceCoins, so maps where monsters come in from more places (each needing its own flowers) pay more: with 0.4, 3 entrances 1.18x, 4 1.32x, 5 1.44x, 8 1.74x. Roads that start at the same spot count as one entrance.
_help.economy.uprootRefund: Share of the coins poured into a flower (planting + upgrades, not healing) you get back when you dig it up. uprootSeconds = how long you hold the key to dig.
_help.juice: Extra effects that don't change the game: damage numbers, hit squash, death pops, confetti, coin counter bounce, short freeze (hit-stop) on bombs and boss kills. They are always on in the game; set any to false here to drop just that one (enabled: false drops them all).
_help.player.bombGap: Seconds before a cat can throw again after a bomb, so a cat with two bombs doesn't throw both by accident.
_help.player.sprint: Holding sprint multiplies speed by sprintSpeed for up to sprintSeconds; stamina refills fully in sprintRecoverSeconds after a sprintRecoverDelay pause. Running dry means waiting until it is a third full.
_help.cats: Character classes. Every number is a multiplier on the player section (1 = normal). growSpeed is how fast a cat pours into flowers (upgrading and healing); upgradeCost is how many coins it pays per coin of progress (0.7 = 30% cheaper). Two players can't pick the same cat.
_help.waves: Which enemies can appear: fromWave = first wave it shows up (or [lo, hi]: a random wave in that range, rolled once per game), weight = how often it is picked, cost = how much of the wave budget one group uses, group = how many spawn together.
_help.waveSets: Other lists like waves, for maps that name one with waveSet in maps.json; maps without one use waves. rush (Hourglass, Four Junctions, Lattice, Five Fords): fast monsters and ones Frostbloom can't hold, a few flyers at an unknown wave, small wasp packs late. wild (Twin Whirls, Bramblewood): leapers and diggers that get past ground flowers, beetles that punish chip damage, flyers rare and late.
_help.enemies.slowResist: Share of a Frostbloom's slow it shrugs off (0.5 = half as slowed: a slow to 25% speed becomes 62.5%).
_help.enemies.dash.leap: During each dash it is in the air: ground-only flowers and poison clouds can't touch it.
_help.enemies.noShield: A boss that never raises a boss shield (its own abilities are enough).
_help.enemies.heals: Mends monsters within radius tiles: perSecond health a second plus share of their max health a second.
_help.enemies.quake: Each time it comes up from underground, flowers within radius tiles lose damage health (times wearMultiplierByLevel for their level; max level is immune).
_help.enemies.withers: Flowers within radius tiles lose perSecond health a second (times wearMultiplierByLevel; max level is immune).
_help.enemies.enrage: Speed grows as it loses health, up to maxSpeedMultiplier when nearly dead.
_help.bloom: Bloom abilities (IDEAS R1): flowers at bloom.level get one special ability each. enabled = false switches them all off (and the price bump). upgradePrice multiplies the cost of the upgrade that reaches bloom.level. daisy: every Nth seed splits into `pieces` more seeds at `damage` share, aimed at monsters within `reach` tiles. sunflower: the beam also takes maxHp of the target's max health. firelily: every monster hit burns for `seconds`, taking `share` of the hit's damage per second (ignores armour). stink: monsters in its clouds take `vulnerable` more damage from everything, for `seconds` after leaving. frost: every Nth pulse freezes non-boss monsters for `freeze` seconds. thorn: every Nth pulse reaches `range` times as far and knocks small monsters back `knock` tiles per second. snap: swallows any non-boss monster below `below` of its health.
_help.elites: Elite monsters (IDEAS R2). enabled = false switches them off. Only `types` can be elite, from wave `fromWave`: the chance is `chance` + `chancePerWave` per wave after that, at most `maxChance`; in endless mode (where the monsters are already much tougher) it starts again at `endlessChance` in wave 11 and grows `endlessChancePerWave` a wave up to `endlessMaxChance`. Elites have `hp` times the health and one trait (picked by weight): armoured adds `armor`; swift multiplies speed by `speed`; regenerating heals `perSecond` of its max health a second while not poisoned or burning; frostproof can't be slowed or frozen; splitting breaks into `count` copies with `hp` of a normal one's health. Each elite carries one power-up (by weight), dropped when it dies and gone after `itemSeconds` if nobody picks it up. fertiliser: the flower you stand on gains a level for free. water: flowers within `radius` tiles heal to full and stop wearing for the rest of the wave. sun: the flower you stand on fires `fireRate` times as fast for `seconds`. snow: every non-boss monster freezes for `seconds`.
_help.bossShield: Boss shields (IDEAS R3). enabled = false switches them off. A boss raises a shield when its health falls to each share in `at` (`atBig` for the last wave's boss and endless bosses). While it is up the boss takes `block` less damage from everything but bombs. Each bomb that hits it takes one segment off (`catHits` gives some cats more per bomb); it has `hitsCoop` segments in co-op, `hitsSolo` alone. Broken, the boss is stunned and takes `exposedDamage` more damage for `exposedSeconds`.
_help.difficulty.morePlayers: Online games can have 3 or 4 cats. For each number of cats: waveSize and enemyHp multiply the co-op wave size and monster health (coopWaveSize, coopEnemyHp), and shieldHits more bomb hits break a boss shield. Tuned with the autopilot so 3 and 4 cats end about like 2 (the third cat helps more than the fourth).
_help.sprint: Sprint mode (chosen on the pick screen, like Hard): a short game of waves.length waves. Each one plays like the normal wave it names (health, size, monsters, bosses on every bossEvery-th), so a Sprint skips the easy middle. The first wave comes after firstWaveDelay seconds, the breaks are timeBetweenWaves long, and to make up for the skipped waves cats start with startCoins times the usual coins and monsters drop coinDrops times as many. After a win, endless carries on from wave 11's numbers.
_help.score: The score on the end screen and in the copied result: perWave for every wave cleared, perCottage for each point of cottage health left, perKill for every monster, all times hard on Hard. Only compare scores of the same mode, map and number of players (a challenge code fixes the first two).
_help.bossChest: Boss chests (IDEAS R3). enabled = false switches them off. A wave in which a boss died ends with a chest: the game pauses and each cat picks one of `choices` random perks; for the first `lockSeconds` nothing can be picked, so keys pressed while finishing the wave don't take one by accident. A perk can be taken at most `maxEach` times (team perks by the whole team, the others by each cat). roof: the cottage gains `cottage` health, up to its max. roots: flowers wear `wear` times as fast. stems: aphids chew `aphids` times as hard. fourth: one more flower type in your loadout. thumb: your planting, upgrades and healing cost `price` times as much. paws: you grow and heal `growSpeed` times as fast. pouch: you carry `bombs` more bombs and they recharge `recharge` times as long.

scout.name: Zip
scout.desc: Very fast, light taps, endless sprint

fourth.name: Another flower
fourth.desc: One more flower type in your loadout

thumb.name: Green thumb
thumb.desc: Your flowers cost 15% less to plant, grow and heal

pouch.name: Bomb pouch
pouch.desc: One more bomb, and bombs recharge 25% faster

sunflower.name: Sunflower
sunflower.desc: Blasts the toughest monster nearest the cottage

firelily.name: Fire Lily
firelily.desc: Fireballs pierce a line of monsters

stink.name: Stinkbloom
stink.desc: Stacking poison clouds that ignore armour (ground)

snap.name: Snapdragon
snap.desc: Gulps critters, bites chunks off big ones (ground)

swarm: Tiny bugs in big packs. Thornrose, Stinkbloom and Fire Lily hit many at once
runner: Very fast. Frostbloom slows them down
dasher: They put on sudden bursts of speed
flyer: They fly straight to the cottage. Only Daisy, Fire Lily and Sunflower can hit them
splitter: They burst into fast little bloblings. Keep some flowers near the cottage
aphid: They stop to chew your flowers. Hold heal on bitten flowers
shield: Heavy armour. Snapdragon bites, Sunflower and poison get through it
mole: They dig under the ground where flowers can't hit them
tank: Slow and very tough. Snapdragon and Sunflower bite through
healer: They mend the monsters around them. Take them out first
hive: Tough, and they keep letting out swarm bugs
wasp: Fast flyers in packs. Only Daisy, Fire Lily and Sunflower can hit them
woolly: Thick fur: Frostbloom can't slow them. Hit them hard and early
hopper: They leap over ground flowers. Daisy and Fire Lily hit them mid-air
charger: Armoured, and they run faster when hurt. Stinkbloom poison seeps through; Snapdragon, Fire Lily and Sunflower crack them
boss: Huge and armoured: small hits do little. Sunflower and Snapdragon bite through
moleking: A boss that digs underground and shakes the flowers near it when it comes up
witch: A boss that heals monsters near it and withers your flowers. Take it down fast
